lines.text: of human morals and manners, for the emancipation and
enrichment of the human mind, and for human culture.
But such phenomena constitute neither miracle nor proof.
They furnish no proof; for one might say (and it is in fact
said that Christianity had great significance for a certain
epoch of history, but all that is over now and done with.
Nor do they constitute the miraculous; for all spiritual and
psychic forces work out their due effects in history, and every-
one is influenced by them whether he is aware of it or not.
But these things do not call for a decision nor are they
offensive. Miracles, properly speaking, are only those events
which essentially cannot be classified within natural and
historical sequences, and which in the natural historical
process stand out as arousing the sentiments of wonder,
astonishment and repulsion. A miracle of such a kind
isquite simply-every straightforward manifestation of
Christian love, which strikes us, shames us, convulses our
being, and yet quickens us.
A miracle is in fact every deed-though it is not strictly
speaking a human deed—and every event which takes place
where the Spirit and mind of Christ hold sway. And where
does Christ hold sway? Wherever the Word of the Gospel is
preached and heard in faith. And for this reason the most
important element in the answer of Jesus, and in the light
of which alone the other affirmations are intelligible, is this:
the poor have good news preached to them. For it cannot be
denied that there are deeds which are inspired by nothing
other than the proclamation of the Gospel of Christ; such
deeds have arisen not from natural impulses, or from moral
considerations, or from the intention of serving the common
good and bettering human conditions, but simply and solely
from love, the love which the Gospel of Christ awakens in the
human heart. These deeds do not propose to change the
world, nor are they done with a view to the effect which
they will have on the world's life; they in fact happen because
the Word of the Gospel has commanded them—nay, has
liberated the spirit of man to perform them.
